readme: Authoritative allowlist of what a team may submit to the SAINTCON AppSec scoring harness. The bridge console (bridge/harness.py) packages a whole-repo snapshot that contains ONLY the source files matched here. Everything else is 'fixed infrastructure' the harness rebuilds from its own pristine baseline: you cannot add a new kind of file, change the Docker build, or install extra packages through a submission. Fix the vulns by editing the existing source in place. The scoring harness enforces the same allowlist on its side; this file is the shared contract.
sourceExtensionsNote: Lowercase, dot-prefixed. C/C++ -> FMM, DNSM. Java -> IPM. Go -> KVS, OTA. Scala -> LOG. Python -> MQB, bridge, tooling. JS/HTML/CSS -> MTA and the console frontends. A file must match one of these (and live outside excludeDirs) to be included in the snapshot.
excludeDirsNote: Never walked. 'vendor' and 'node_modules' are the important ones for the allowlist: they hold third-party packages shipped as source, so without pruning them the .go/.js rule would sweep them back in. 'secrets' must never leave the deployment; the rest are VCS/build/cache noise.

fixedByBaseline.note: These are NOT part of a submission. The harness always uses its baseline copy, so editing them changes nothing about your score. Listed for clarity, not enforced by name -- the allowlist above is what decides.
